shipped_rows.title_o: The dark side of self-and social perception: black uniforms and aggression in professional sports

blind_target.authors: Webster, G. D., Urland, G. R., & Correll, J.
blind_target.title: Can uniform color color aggression? Quasi-experimental evidence from professional ice hockey
blind_target.evidence_quote: We now extend our investigation to the modern NHL while attempting to address deficiencies in past research which supported the black uniforms-heightened aggression connection.
blind_target.outcome_quote: Also, we failed to find support for reduced aggression when wearing white uniforms (Webster et al., 2012) as we conducted comparisons within teams across eight seasons while ensuring the overall aggression in the league remained consistent (thus avoiding a history threat).
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Study III directly addresses the modern NHL black-uniform and white-uniform findings, discusses methodological deficiencies in Webster, and reports failure for the white effect as well as the nested black-uniform analysis.

luna_triage.reason: Study III directly retests Webster et al.'s NHL result, describing the finding of greater aggression/penalties in black uniforms and reporting that its own within-team analyses failed to support the white-uniform contrast. The shipped row 2625 is Frank and Gilovich (1988), a different original; Webster et al. (2012) is separately cited with its own title and DOI and is not represented by that row.
